items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8420            Revised 5/26/2020

SPONSOR: GOUNARDES
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the retirement and social security law, the education
law, the public authorities law and the administrative code of the city
of New York, in relation to establishing a coronavirus disease 2019
(COVID-19) presumption for public employee death benefits; and providing
for the repeal of such provisions upon the expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of this bill is to establish a COVID-19 presumption to
provide accidental death benefits to public employees who reported to
work or an alternate worksite and subsequently died due to COVID-19.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill amends Article 2 of the retirement and social
security law to establish a COVID-19 presumption for accidental death
benefits for tier I and II members of the New York state employees'
retirement system (NYSERS) who reported to their usual place of work or
an alternate worksite which was not their place of residence, as
directed by a public employer, on or after March 1, 2020 and contracted
coronavirus, COVID-19, or SARS-COV2, or equivalent subsequently, as
confirmed by a positive lab test or diagnosis, within 45 days from
reporting to work and subsequently died from COVID-19, as indicated on
such member's death certificate or as determined by a health care
professional. Such accidental death benefit amount shall be reduced by
any ordinary death benefits amount. This section would also permit the
beneficiaries of any retired member of such retirement system, who
retired on or after March 1, 2020, and had reported to work prior to
retirement, contracted coronavirus, COVID-19, or SARS-COV2, and subse-
quently died from COVID-19, as indicated on such member's death certif-
icate or as determined by a health care professional, to apply for a
conversion of such member's service or disability retirement benefit to
an accidental death benefit.

security law to establish a COVID-19 presumption for accidental death
benefits for tier I, II, Ill, V or VI members of the New York state
police and fire retirement system (NYSPFRS) who reported to their usual

JUSTIFICATION:

History will remember New York's essential workforce as the true heroes
of the 2020 coronavirus pandemic. Performing jobs so critical to the
functioning of society that they are precluded from the ability to tele-
commute, many of the essential employees in America's hardest-hit state
include civil servants such as nurses, emergency medical service person-
nel, teachers, transit employees, police officers and firefighters.

When these essential public workers fall ill on the job, their benefici-
aries are entitled to an ordinary death benefit paid out of their
retirement system which is generally three times their final average
salary (FAS). If the worker can prove that the accident was job-related,
however, he or she is entitled to a much larger amount called the acci-
dental death benefit which provides 50% of the employee's FAS each year
for the lifetime of the beneficiary. For certain uniformed titles enti-
tled to an additional Special Accidental Death Benefit, the benefit
amount is 100% FAS. In order to access this larger death benefit, howev-
er, civil servants will generally need to prove that the illness or
accident was incurred as a direct result of performance of duty - an
impossible standard for a disease as pervasive as COVID-19.

This bill helps New York State's civil servants qualify for an acci-
dental death benefit by shifting the burden of proof from the employee
to the employer, who must prove by competent evidence that the
contraction of COVID-19 was NOT job-related if they want to deny the
civil servant the accidental death benefit. In order to qualify for the
presumption, the public employee must have reported to work anytime on
or after March 1st, 2020, and then contracted COVID-19 within 45 days of
their last day. If after this contraction the employee passes away, and
a medical professional is able to list COVID-19 as a contributing factor
in such employee's death, it is presumed that the death was a natural
and proximate result of an accident sustained in the line of duty and
not a result of willful negligence on the part of the decedent.

A common feature of pension law, presumptions are most commonly used
when there is a strong link between a given disease and the hazardous
nature of the job most likely to cause it (i.e. firefighters and cancer,
or most famously participation in the 9/11 cleanup and certain respir-
atory and gastroesophageal diseases). Given the ubiquitous spread of the
latest strain of coronavirus, there can be no argument that anyone
forced to report to work during the pandemic who later fell ill
contracted the disease as a direct result of such reporting. Providing
adequate death benefits for the families of these fallen heroes, then,
is the very least we can do to honor their public service. It is by
their sacrifice that the rest of us were kept safe.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately and shall be deemed to have been
in full force and effect on and after March 1, 2020; provided that this
act shall remain in effect until the later of December 31, 2020, or the
date of the expiration order number 202, dated March 7, 2020, as amended
and extended, and shall expire and be deemed repealed on such date.

summary: Establish a coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) presumption for public employee death benefits where a member was required to physically report to work; did in fact physically report to work as of March first, two thousand twenty; contracted COVID-19; and where the applicable head of the member's retirement system or such system's medical board determines COVID-19 to have been a  significant contributing factor in the member's death.
